board.canonical_name: Safe, Auditable Agent Execution in Martech Systems
Governance and Review of Generative Marketing Content at Volume
Governed Semantic Context Layer for Agents and Activation
Provable Downstream Consent, Deletion and Purpose Enforcement

proposals.name: AI-mediated demand is dark to measurement
proposals.definition: A growing share of research, comparison and even purchase intent now forms inside assistants (ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Overviews, Copilot, Perplexity) that emit no query, no impression count, and often no referrer, so teams cannot size, trend, or value the channel that increasingly precedes the click.
proposals.why_unsolved: There is no telemetry primitive to instrument. Assistant surfaces are not publishers with an analytics contract: referrers are stripped or collapsed into a generic host, prompts are never exposed, and the majority of exposure produces no visit at all, so even perfect landing-page analytics measures the wrong denominator. Search Console-style blending mixes AI surfaces into existing buckets rather than separating them, and no vendor can reconstruct the impression side because it lives in a private inference log. Self-reported attribution surveys are the current workaround, which is an admission that the instrumentation does not exist.
proposals.evidence: Live now because the substitution is visible on the other side of the ledger: informational and mid-funnel organic traffic has been eroding across categories while brand demand holds or rises, producing a measurement gap that shows up as unexplained 'direct' and unattributable brand search. Budget decisions are being made in 2026 with no defensible number for a channel practitioners agree is material.

proposals.name: Black-box platform optimization has broken incrementality testing
proposals.definition: Ad platforms have consolidated buying into opaque, cross-inventory campaign types (Performance Max, Advantage+, and their CTV/retail equivalents) that reallocate spend across placements internally, which destroys the stable 'channel' abstraction that MMM, geo experiments and holdouts depend on.
proposals.why_unsolved: Two blockers compound. First, the unit of control no longer matches the unit of measurement: you can hold out a geo but you cannot hold the platform's internal mix constant, so the treatment is undefined and results are not reproducible across periods. Second, the platform's optimizer is adversarial to the test — it preferentially finds users who would have converted anyway and, when a holdout is imposed, re-optimizes into the remaining cells, biasing lift upward. Platform-run lift tools are self-graded and underpowered; open-source MMM (Meridian, Robyn) still needs granular spend and reach inputs that these campaign types no longer report. There is no third party with the log-level access required to referee.
proposals.evidence: Live because the migration to consolidated campaign types became effectively mandatory across the largest platforms in 2025-26 while granular placement reporting was simultaneously reduced. Teams that had working geo-test programs two years ago report that results stopped replicating, which is a different complaint from the perennial 'attribution is hard.'

proposals.name: No identity or authorization primitive for agent traffic
proposals.definition: When an autonomous agent browses, compares, fills a form or completes a checkout on a user's behalf, the site sees an unauthenticated non-human client with no consent record, no CRM linkage, no payment credential of its own and no way to prove whose behalf it acts on.
proposals.why_unsolved: The stack forces a false choice: bot management blocks the agent (losing the sale) or allows it (losing fraud protection, personalization, consent capture and attribution simultaneously). Emerging protocol work — MCP for tool access, agent-payment and agentic-commerce specs from the payment networks and platform vendors — solves credential handoff for a single vendor's walled path, not open-web recognition. Nobody has resolved delegated consent (whose lawful basis covers the agent's data collection), delegated identity (which customer record to attach), or liability for agent-initiated errors. Until a signed-agent-identity standard is adopted on both the client and the CDN/bot-mitigation side, every implementation is bespoke.
proposals.evidence: Live because agent-driven checkout moved from demo to shipped feature in 2025-26 and merchants are now making binary allow/block decisions at the edge without the data to evaluate them. The tell is that the same traffic is simultaneously classified as valuable by ecommerce teams and as an attack by security teams inside the same company.

proposals.name: Consent-to-use lineage and unlearning for AI systems
proposals.definition: Marketers now feed first-party data into embeddings, fine-tunes, retrieval indexes, vendor-hosted models and agent prompts, but consent frameworks record purposes ('analytics', 'advertising') that do not map to 'model training' or 'inference', and no system tracks which records reached which artifact.
proposals.why_unsolved: The blocker is architectural, not legal-interpretive. CMPs capture purpose at collection; CDPs and warehouses propagate identifiers but not purpose-level constraints; feature stores, vector databases and vendor fine-tunes are downstream sinks with no lineage back to the consent event. A deletion or objection request can be honored in the CRM and the warehouse and still be irrecoverable from an embedding index or a trained weight set — machine unlearning has no production-grade implementation, so the only compliant answer is retraining, which nobody does per-request. Vendor DPAs increasingly disclaim training use, but there is no verification mechanism.
proposals.evidence: Live because the collision of three things is new: near-universal US state privacy coverage with purpose-limitation and sensitive-data rules, EU AI Act obligations phasing in through 2026, and the fact that 2025 was the year marketing teams actually put customer data into retrieval systems at scale. Legal review is now the rate limiter on personalization projects, which was not true in 2023.

proposals.name: Content verification is the bottleneck AI generation created
proposals.definition: Generation capacity is effectively free while the human capacity to verify claims, check regulatory and legal exposure, confirm brand-voice fidelity and detect near-duplicate output has not increased, so the constraint has moved from producing content to being willing to publish it.
proposals.why_unsolved: There is no verification layer with usable precision. Fact-checking a claim against an authoritative internal source requires that source to exist as structured, current, machine-readable truth — most organizations' claims substantiation lives in PDFs and people's heads. Automated brand-voice and compliance scoring is itself model-based, so it fails on exactly the subtle cases that matter and produces enough false positives that reviewers stop trusting it. Provenance standards (C2PA) address whether an asset was AI-made, not whether it is accurate or approved. The result is a queue at legal/medical/regulatory review that scales with output volume, plus growing cleanup cost from published errors.
proposals.evidence: Live because the failure mode has flipped: 2023-24 complaints were about output quality, 2025-26 complaints are about review throughput, retraction, and the discovery that large libraries of AI-assisted pages contain unverifiable claims. Organizations are now imposing volume caps for reasons unrelated to cost.

proposals.name: Brand presence inside model outputs: no census measurement, no proven lever
proposals.definition: Teams are asked to manage how their brand appears in assistant answers, but available tooling estimates visibility by sampling synthetic prompts against nondeterministic, personalized, memory- and location-dependent systems, and no causal link has been established between any optimization action and a change in output.
proposals.why_unsolved: You cannot measure a population you cannot enumerate: real user prompts are private, so every 'AI share of voice' number is a sample from a prompt set the vendor invented, with no known relationship to actual demand distribution. Outputs vary run to run, by account history, by which retrieval index and model version served the request, and vendors change models without notice, so time series confound intervention with silent model churn. There is no experimental design available — no A/B, no holdout, no crawl-and-index feedback loop equivalent to what SEO had. So the discipline currently consists of plausible heuristics with no way to falsify them.
proposals.evidence: Live because a whole vendor category and a job title appeared in 2025-26 on top of this unresolved measurement base, and because practitioners running the same tracker on the same brand report material week-over-week swings that correspond to model updates rather than anything they did.

proposals.name: No governed context layer for marketing agents to act on
proposals.definition: Agents can only be trusted to plan, spend or message if they can resolve what a customer, an audience, a conversion and a margin-positive outcome mean; that definitional layer is currently scattered across a BI semantic model, a CDP's audience logic, ad platform conversion configs and tribal knowledge, and no two agree.
proposals.why_unsolved: The blocker is that identity resolution and metric definition are re-implemented independently in every tool, so there is no single artifact an agent can read. Warehouse-native/composable stacks moved storage but not semantics; semantic layers cover BI reads, not activation writes or permissioned action. MCP-style connectors expose tools without exposing meaning or guardrails, so an agent gets write access to spend before it gets a trustworthy definition of ROAS. There is also no evaluation harness: no accepted way to regression-test an agent's marketing decisions, no rollback for actions taken in third-party systems, and no audit trail linking an outcome to the agent decision that caused it. That is why agent pilots stall at pilot.
proposals.evidence: Live because 2025-26 procurement shifted to agent-branded products across ESPs, ad platforms and CDPs, while the observable adoption pattern is drafting and summarization rather than autonomous action — a gap explained by missing context and missing evals, not by model capability.

proposals.name: Cross-platform dedup and quality control in retail media and walled-garden clean rooms
proposals.definition: Retail media, CTV and platform clean rooms permit aggregate querying but not the cross-party joins needed to deduplicate reach and frequency or to compare incrementality on a common basis, and the open supply feeding these buys now includes large volumes of AI-generated inventory that verification cannot classify quickly enough.
proposals.why_unsolved: Clean rooms are designed to prevent exactly the operation measurement requires: aggregation thresholds and query review block the row-level overlap needed for reach dedup, and there is no shared join key across retailers or between retailers and the large platforms. IAB standards for retail media measurement are voluntary and each network's incrementality methodology is self-defined and non-comparable, so a portfolio-level answer does not exist. On the supply side, classification of made-for-advertising and AI-generated sites is a moving target that generation cost has made asymmetric; curated marketplaces are the practical response but reintroduce opacity about what was actually bought.
proposals.evidence: Live because retail media budgets crossed the threshold where CFOs demand portfolio-level comparison, and because the volume of low-quality generated inventory in open programmatic grew sharply through 2025 while inclusion-list curation became the default mitigation — a workaround, not a fix.

proposals.name: Measuring demand created inside AI assistants
proposals.definition: Marketers cannot reliably size, attribute, or optimize the demand that originates in ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity and AI Overviews, because most of the influence happens in an answer that never produces a click and the clicks that do occur arrive stripped of usable source data.
proposals.why_unsolved: There is no Search Console equivalent for assistants: no impression, prompt, or citation logs are exposed to brands, referrers are often absent or normalized (so a large share of assistant referrals land in GA4 as 'direct'), and in-answer mentions that drive later branded search or direct navigation generate no event at all. UTM tagging cannot fix a channel where the intermediary decides whether a link exists. Vendors sell proxies (server-log crawler analysis, referrer regex lists, synthetic prompt panels), none of which reconcile to a source of truth.
proposals.evidence: 2026 practitioner content is dominated by 'LLM traffic attribution' workarounds citing ~70% of AI-referred sessions misclassified in GA4, and enterprise GEO tooling roundups from early 2026 openly flag that measurement, not tactics, is the procurement blocker. The problem got sharper in 2026 as assistants added in-answer shopping and summarization, moving conversion earlier than any brand-owned instrumentation.

proposals.name: Incrementality inside black-box buying and retail media
proposals.definition: With spend concentrated in automated products (Performance Max, Advantage+, retail media self-service) marketers cannot establish what portion of reported conversions is incremental, nor compare ROAS across networks whose attribution rules differ.
proposals.why_unsolved: The optimizer, the attribution engine, and the reporting layer are all owned by the seller, and log-level or segment-level data is withheld; each retail media network uses its own window and view-through logic. Clean geo/holdout experiments are corrupted because cross-campaign automation reallocates budget into the holdout, and MMM calibration requires the experiments that platforms make hardest to run. Clean rooms restrict the joins and query granularity needed for causal work.
proposals.evidence: 2026 industry surveys: ~55-57% of US advertisers name lack of retail media measurement standardization as their top challenge, and a 2026 Skai/Stratably study found 75% cite incrementality as the biggest problem while only ~15% feel effective at measuring it; a 2026 PPC survey of 1,300+ practitioners found black-box targeting the leading PMax frustration at ~56%.

proposals.name: No valid measurement instrument for AI answer visibility
proposals.definition: The 'AI visibility / GEO' tool category produces share-of-voice and citation scores that are not reproducible, not comparable across vendors, and not tied to any denominator of real user prompts.
proposals.why_unsolved: Model outputs are non-deterministic, personalized, memory- and location-dependent, and change with silent model updates, so any score is a sample from an unstable distribution. Vendors invent prompt sets rather than sampling actual demand (no prompt-volume data exists the way keyword volume did), and there is no audit standard, so two tools give different answers for the same brand and neither can be validated against outcomes. That makes optimization decisions unfalsifiable.
proposals.evidence: Enterprise buying guides published in 2026 explicitly warn about prompt-set construction and score comparability as procurement caveats, and practitioner writeups this year focus on 'most teams measure this badly and get false confidence' rather than on which tool to buy — a signal the category's validity, not its availability, is the blocker.

proposals.name: Telling humans, agents, and fraud apart
proposals.definition: Web and app analytics, personalization, and conversion data are increasingly polluted by agentic browsers and AI crawlers that behave like logged-in humans, and there is no deployed way to label traffic as human, delegated-agent, or malicious with enough reliability to act on it.
proposals.why_unsolved: User agents are spoofable, IP allowlists are brittle, and agentic browsers execute inside a real user session with real credentials, so they are legitimately not bots but also not human attention. Web Bot Auth (RFC 9421 signatures, IETF WG chartered in 2026) covers only cooperating crawlers and says nothing about user-delegated agents; analytics vendors' IVT filters were built for click fraud, not for assistants. Consequences: inflated or deflated conversion rates, wasted bid signals, broken A/B tests, and personalization served to nobody.
proposals.evidence: Live in 2026: Amazon obtained a preliminary injunction against Perplexity's Comet agent partly on the argument that automated traffic was presented as human; Cloudflare/Akamai/OpenAI/Amazon are standardizing bot attestation; measurement vendors report ~20% invalid traffic rates and are publishing guidance on agentic contamination of attribution.

proposals.name: Consent that does not propagate through the stack
proposals.definition: Teams can capture consent and opt-out signals at the edge but cannot enforce them consistently downstream across pixels, warehouses, reverse-ETL, CDPs, ad platforms, and now AI vendors and model training.
proposals.why_unsolved: Consent is stored as a state in a CMP while data is copied into dozens of systems that have no shared consent schema or revocation path; opt-outs (including Global Privacy Control, now mandatory in a dozen-plus states) must be honored at the tag level and propagated to downstream processors, and no widely deployed plumbing does this end to end. Once first-party data reaches an AI vendor, deletion and 'do not train' obligations have no technical enforcement mechanism.
proposals.evidence: Nearly twenty US state comprehensive laws in force by 2026 with coordinated AG sweeps (CA/CO/CT) specifically targeting sites that claim GPC compliance while still firing retargeting pixels; CIPA/wiretapping class actions have moved from ad trackers onto AI products themselves during 2026, including suits filed as recently as this month over recording and training without consent.

proposals.name: Governing AI agents that write into marketing systems
proposals.definition: There is no dependable control plane for agents that take actions — editing customer records or product attributes, launching campaigns, replying to customers — covering permissions, approval, audit, evaluation, and rollback.
proposals.why_unsolved: MCP and vendor agent frameworks solved connectivity and context but not policy: they carry credentials, not scoped intent, and each SaaS tool has its own permission model with no cross-tool identity for a non-human actor. There is no accepted evaluation harness for marketing agents (what counts as a regression in a brand voice or an offer decision?), no transactional rollback across CRM/ESP/ad platform, and audit trails stop at the API boundary. So teams either keep agents read-only or accept unbounded blast radius.
proposals.evidence: MCP went from niche to near-universal vendor support by early-to-mid 2026 (SDK downloads up roughly 970x in 18 months), which moved the bottleneck from integration to control; 2026 martech architecture coverage now centers on constraining agents that alter customer records and compliance logic, and CMO surveys this year report explainability and value-proof gaps rather than capability gaps.

proposals.name: Agentic checkout severs the customer relationship
proposals.definition: When an AI agent transacts on a shopper's behalf, the merchant frequently loses the identity, consent, and behavioral data that CRM, lifecycle marketing, loyalty, and attribution depend on — and must support competing, incompatible protocols to be present at all.
proposals.why_unsolved: Tokenized agent payments deliberately withhold raw credentials and often withhold contactable identity and marketing permissions; the order arrives without a session, referrer, or opt-in. Competing standards (OpenAI/Stripe's ACP versus Google's UCP/AP2, plus retailer-specific opt-in regimes) force dual implementation with no shared feed, returns, or post-purchase messaging semantics, and platform holders control eligibility. There is no established way to run retention marketing against an agent-mediated buyer.
proposals.evidence: 2026 saw production launches of agentic checkout on both stacks, litigation defining whether retailers can refuse agents (Amazon v. Perplexity, March 2026), Amazon blocking assistant crawlers in robots.txt, and consultancies advising dual-protocol strategies — i.e., the standards war is live and unresolved right now.

proposals.name: Scaling AI content without destroying the asset
proposals.definition: Content teams are asked to publish at AI-enabled volume while having no reliable pre-publication signal for whether output will be rewarded, ignored, or penalized by search and answer engines.
proposals.why_unsolved: Quality classifiers and answer-engine selection criteria are undisclosed and change without notice; feedback is delayed and confounded by site-wide effects, so there is no test loop faster than weeks-to-months at the domain level. Nothing in the tooling links a specific asset to whether an assistant cited it, so the optimization target itself is unobservable (see the visibility measurement problem). The result is volume decisions made on faith, with site-level downside risk.
proposals.evidence: Conductor's 2026 AEO/GEO CMO study of 250+ executives found scaling AI content is the top-ranked strategy across all maturity levels — above structured data and original research — while 2026 search coverage documents ongoing quality-related visibility losses from exactly that tactic.

proposals.name: Causal measurement across fragmented media
proposals.definition: Marketers still cannot reliably determine the incremental effect of spend across walled gardens, offline channels, retail media, and owned touchpoints. Attribution, media-mix modeling, lift tests, and clean-room analyses often produce incompatible answers.
proposals.why_unsolved: There is no shared ground truth: platforms restrict user-level data, identity coverage is incomplete, experiments are not consistently available, and auction dynamics violate common causal assumptions. Neither better modeling nor larger budgets can recover information that platforms do not expose.
proposals.evidence: Signal loss from consent requirements, platform privacy controls, cookie deprecation and partial reprieves, and expanding walled-garden and retail-media spend has made reconciliation—not merely attribution-model selection—the active practitioner problem.

proposals.name: Observability of AI-mediated discovery
proposals.definition: Brands cannot consistently measure or influence how products are discovered, described, recommended, and purchased through AI assistants and answer engines. Traditional search metrics do not capture unlinked answers, synthesized recommendations, or agent-completed journeys.
proposals.why_unsolved: AI interfaces expose little stable impression, query, citation, or downstream-conversion telemetry; outputs vary by model, prompt, user context, and retrieval index. There is also no broadly accepted equivalent of rank, share of voice, or referral attribution across assistants.
proposals.evidence: Customer discovery is shifting from lists of links toward generated answers and agentic interactions, while the surrounding optimization tools largely infer visibility through synthetic prompts rather than platform-supplied audience data.

proposals.name: Durable identity and consent propagation
proposals.definition: Companies cannot maintain a sufficiently accurate customer identity graph while also enforcing each person's consent, purpose restrictions, deletion requests, and regional rules across every activation and analytics system.
proposals.why_unsolved: Identifiers are probabilistic, mutable, and channel-specific; household and person identities are easily conflated; and downstream platforms interpret consent differently. Consent signals and deletion events do not propagate with reliable lineage through exports, clean rooms, models, and vendor copies.
proposals.evidence: First-party-data programs have expanded the number of copies and destinations for customer data just as privacy enforcement, consent-mode requirements, and restrictions on sensitive-data use have tightened.

proposals.name: Semantic and quality control for marketing data
proposals.definition: Even well-funded teams cannot keep event definitions, campaign taxonomies, product identifiers, customer states, and revenue metrics consistent across warehouses, CDPs, ad platforms, analytics tools, and AI systems.
proposals.why_unsolved: Schema ownership is distributed, vendor APIs change, client-side instrumentation breaks, transformations obscure lineage, and business definitions evolve. Observability tools can flag anomalies but usually cannot determine the intended business meaning or repair historical comparability.
proposals.evidence: Warehouse-native and composable stacks have increased flexibility but also multiplied transformations and owners. Generative analytics and automated decisioning now amplify semantic errors that previously affected only dashboards.

proposals.name: Comparable retail-media measurement
proposals.definition: Advertisers cannot obtain deduplicated, comparable measurement of reach, incrementality, and profit across retail-media networks while separating genuine demand creation from purchases that would have occurred anyway.
proposals.why_unsolved: Each retailer controls transaction data, inventory, identity matching, attribution windows, and metric definitions. Clean rooms permit selected analyses but do not create neutral standards, expose full auction data, or deduplicate shoppers reliably across retailers.
proposals.evidence: Retail media has expanded from a few dominant networks into many retailer, marketplace, delivery, and commerce-media offerings, making inconsistent self-reported measurement a larger budget-allocation problem.

proposals.name: Governed generative-content operations
proposals.definition: Marketing organizations cannot generate and distribute content at scale while reliably guaranteeing factual accuracy, brand consistency, rights clearance, disclosure, localization quality, and regulatory compliance.
proposals.why_unsolved: Models are nondeterministic, source and training-data rights are often unverifiable, automated evaluators miss contextual failures, and approval requirements vary by market and claim type. Human review restores confidence but removes much of the promised speed and cost advantage.
proposals.evidence: The bottleneck has moved from generating copy and images to approving, tracing, and safely publishing thousands of variants, especially in regulated industries and global campaigns.

proposals.name: Interoperable privacy-safe data collaboration
proposals.definition: Brands, publishers, retailers, and platforms cannot collaborate on audience and outcome data through a portable workflow that is both analytically useful and demonstrably privacy-safe.
proposals.why_unsolved: Clean rooms differ in identity support, query languages, privacy controls, permitted use cases, and activation endpoints. Low match rates and privacy thresholds weaken analysis, while governance depends on contractual controls and operator behavior as much as technical isolation.
proposals.evidence: Clean-room adoption has grown, but practitioners still rebuild analyses for each partner and often discover that nominally available data cannot answer the intended question or support activation.

proposals.name: Reliable autonomous cross-channel optimization
proposals.definition: Marketing systems cannot safely optimize budgets, bids, audiences, messages, and contact policies across channels against long-term business outcomes without intensive human supervision.
proposals.why_unsolved: Platforms optimize local proxy objectives and withhold decision data; delayed outcomes and channel interference make global reward estimation unstable. Agents also lack dependable constraints for brand policy, inventory, margin, consent, and customer fatigue, and cannot explain many consequential actions.
proposals.evidence: Agentic marketing products are moving from content assistance toward campaign execution, but production deployments remain bounded by approval gates, narrow scopes, and rollback controls because proxy gaming and compounding errors remain common risks.

proposals.name: Cross-channel causal measurement that finance can trust
proposals.definition: Marketers still cannot reliably determine the incremental business effect of spending across search, social, CTV, creators, retail media, offline channels and AI-mediated journeys.
proposals.why_unsolved: Exposure and outcome data remain trapped in proprietary platforms, identifiers are disappearing, outcome definitions differ, and newer channels are poorly represented in models. Consequently, MTA, experiments and MMM frequently produce conflicting answers, with no accepted method for reconciling them.
proposals.evidence: IAB’s 2026 State of Data describes advanced measurement as being at a breaking point because of signal loss, inconsistent data and underrepresented channels. IAB launched Project Eidos specifically because shared constructs and comparable, privacy-ready methods still do not exist; cross-platform measurement is a heightened priority for 72% of surveyed buyers in 2026. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/IAB_StateofDataReport_February_2026pdf.pdf?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: A trustworthy, machine-usable marketing context layer
proposals.definition: Companies lack a continuously accurate layer combining customer identity, product and content data, consent, brand rules, taxonomy and business definitions that humans and AI agents can use consistently.
proposals.why_unsolved: Connectors move records but do not reconcile conflicting identities, meanings, freshness requirements or permissions across CRM, CDP, analytics, commerce and unstructured repositories. Walled gardens compound the problem, while probabilistic agents amplify small data and semantic errors into customer-facing actions.
proposals.evidence: BCG’s 2026 CMO survey identifies data foundations, brand-intelligence layers and multi-agent orchestration as the infrastructure separating superficial AI adoption from operational transformation. Salesforce’s agentic-marketing research lists data integrity as a leading adoption concern, while Adobe/IDC says siloed customer data deprives agents of the context needed for reliable action. ([bcg.com](https://www.bcg.com/publications/2026/making-the-agentic-marketing-transformation-a-reality?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Safe control of autonomous marketing agents
proposals.definition: Marketing teams cannot yet delegate campaign changes, media purchases, customer interactions or content publication to agents with dependable limits, observability and accountability.
proposals.why_unsolved: Agents are nondeterministic and may delegate to other agents or tools, but the ecosystem lacks mature standards for machine identity, scoped authority, action logs, approval thresholds, rollback and responsibility across vendor boundaries. Human review catches some errors but eliminates much of the promised speed and scale.
proposals.evidence: Only 8% of CMOs in BCG’s 2026 survey reported campaigns where multiple agents operate autonomously. Salesforce found security, data exposure, compliance, integrity and visibility into AI actions constraining adoption; meanwhile, IAB Tech Lab’s AAMP protocols are still being developed, showing that the control plane is not yet settled. ([bcg.com](https://www.bcg.com/publications/2026/making-the-agentic-marketing-transformation-a-reality?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: End-to-end enforcement of privacy choices
proposals.definition: A brand cannot reliably guarantee that a consumer’s consent, opt-out, deletion or sensitive-data restrictions are honored across every site, app, SDK, data partner, clean room and activation platform.
proposals.why_unsolved: Consent-management platforms often record a choice without enforcing it throughout downstream infrastructure. Account linkage, guest sessions, mobile SDKs, partner reuse and differing jurisdictional rules create propagation failures that are difficult to detect or prove retrospectively.
proposals.evidence: The 2026 digital-experience analytics survey found that four in ten Fortune 1000 companies still lacked a CMP and emphasized that even deployed CMPs must be tested for actual tag and ecosystem enforcement. IAB introduced a newly amended multi-state agreement effective June 2, 2026, while regulators are testing end-to-end propagation of privacy signals through accounts and mobile SDKs. ([cardinalpath.com](https://www.cardinalpath.com/wp-content/uploads/2026_State_of_Digital_Experience-Analytics.pdf?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Decision-grade measurement of AI discovery
proposals.definition: Brands cannot reliably measure how often AI answer engines mention, cite, recommend or misrepresent them—or connect that exposure to downstream revenue.
proposals.why_unsolved: Outputs vary by model, prompt, location, personalization and repeated run; platforms disclose neither the true query universe nor complete exposure and referral logs. Vendors therefore sample proprietary prompt sets and produce incompatible scores, while no durable identifier connects an AI answer to later branded search, direct traffic or purchase.
proposals.evidence: IAB reported in August 2026 that more than 20 AI-visibility vendors use differing methods that can return different answers for the same brand; its new framework distinguishes merely directional data from decision-grade measurement. Research also shows that one-off visibility values are statistically unstable, and IAB explicitly identifies downstream attribution as unfinished standardization work. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/guidelines/measuring-visibility-in-the-ai-era/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Comparable incrementality across commerce and retail media networks
proposals.definition: Advertisers cannot compare the incremental sales impact of retail and commerce media investments across networks, or cleanly separate advertising effects from promotions, organic demand and retailer merchandising.
proposals.why_unsolved: Each network controls its transaction data, audience construction, attribution windows and control-group methodology. There is no broadly implemented mechanism for cross-network deduplication, consistent counterfactuals or auditing platform-reported returns against total business results.
proposals.evidence: IAB and IAB Europe issued incrementality guidelines only in late 2025, and IAB’s 2026 work continues to call for common standards based on true causal impact. FMI’s 2026 initiative similarly describes the lack of common retail-media measurement standards as a continuing industry challenge rather than a solved implementation issue. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/guidelines/guidelines-for-incremental-measurement-in-commerce-media/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Verifiable provenance, rights and brand integrity for synthetic creative
proposals.definition: At generative-production scale, marketers cannot reliably prove how every asset was made, whether its inputs and likenesses were authorized, or whether the finished claim remains accurate and on-brand after adaptation and distribution.
proposals.why_unsolved: Provenance metadata can be removed during screenshots, transcoding or platform processing, and a valid provenance record proves processing history—not truth, rights clearance or brand approval. Disclosure requirements and platform implementations also remain inconsistent, leaving asset-level governance dependent on fragile workflow controls.
proposals.evidence: IAB released its first AI advertising disclosure framework in January 2026, while Google changed its ad-labeling capabilities in July, indicating that operating rules are still forming. C2PA adoption is expanding, but independent 2026 research found that its current specification does not satisfy all security goals required for high-stakes verification. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/news/iab-releases-industrys-first-ai-transparency-and-disclosure-framework-to-guide-responsible-advertising-in-a-generative-ai-landscape/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Interoperable product discovery and attribution for agentic commerce
proposals.definition: Brands cannot ensure that shopping agents receive accurate, real-time product information, represent the brand correctly and preserve attribution when discovery and checkout occur outside brand-controlled interfaces.
proposals.why_unsolved: Commerce agents and platforms use competing protocols and interpretations of product attributes, offers, inventory and trust signals. No widely adopted standard preserves agent identity, recommendation context, consent and attribution through comparison, handoff, checkout and post-purchase activity.
proposals.evidence: NIQ’s 2026 commerce report identifies interoperability among competing Western protocols as a structural challenge. Visa’s 2026 agentic-commerce study calls for common standards and brand-owned attribution, while OpenAttribution’s commerce profile was still a draft under public review in June–July 2026; IAB also lists agentic-commerce attribution as future standards work. ([nielseniq.com](https://nielseniq.com/global/en/insights/report/2026/commerce-trends-intelligence/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Agentic Bot Traffic Distorting Top-of-Funnel Attribution
proposals.definition: Autonomous AI agents and web scrapers executing research queries mimic human engagement metrics, inflating web visits and lead indicators without buying intent.
proposals.why_unsolved: Heuristics and CAPTCHAs cannot reliably differentiate between authorized user-delegated procurement agents, competitor scraping LLMs, and genuine human browsing without degrading conversion friction.
proposals.evidence: Marketing analytics teams report unprecedented divergence between session volumes and downstream sales velocity following broad adoption of autonomous AI browsing assistants.

proposals.name: Cross-Clean-Room Signal Fragmentation Across Walled Gardens
proposals.definition: Brands operating across multiple ad networks cannot compute unified cross-publisher deduplicated reach, frequency, or incremental lift without exposing raw PII.
proposals.why_unsolved: Ad platforms enforce non-interoperable cryptographic schemas and differential privacy noise budgets, making cross-clean-room multi-party computation mathematically or commercially prohibited.
proposals.evidence: Enterprise advertisers running concurrent retail media networks and mega-platform campaigns have duplicate conversion attribution exceeding actual revenue by 30 to 50 percent.

proposals.name: Multi-Agent Autonomous Campaign State Drift and Race Conditions
proposals.definition: Autonomous MarTech agents executing micro-optimizations across bidding, creative variant generation, and audience segmentation trigger conflicting feedback loops.
proposals.why_unsolved: No standardized distributed consensus or shared state management protocol exists across disparate vendor APIs, causing agents to continuously counteract each other's parameter updates.
proposals.evidence: Teams deploying multiple autonomous optimization tools simultaneously report erratic budget swings and self-cannibalizing keyword bid spikes during automated real-time bidding events.

proposals.name: Real-Time Generative Asset Provenance and Brand Safety Auditing
proposals.definition: Dynamically generated, personalized generative content variants cannot be pre-audited for subtle hallucinated claims, trademark drift, or tone violations at millisecond serving latency.
proposals.why_unsolved: In-line multi-modal verification models introduce significant latency overhead that breaks real-time ad serving and dynamic content assembly SLAs.
proposals.evidence: Regulated industries such as financial services and healthcare continue to restrict automated on-the-fly generative personalization to static pre-approved template slots.

proposals.name: Zero-Copy Warehouse Query Latency for High-Throughput Personalization
proposals.definition: Composable MarTech architectures reading directly from enterprise data warehouses fail to deliver sub-50ms read/write response times for high-concurrency real-time edge triggers.
proposals.why_unsolved: Cloud data warehouses and lakehouses are fundamentally architected for analytical batch/micro-batch processing rather than extreme-concurrency low-latency operational transactional workloads.
proposals.evidence: Engineering teams adopting composable CDPs still maintain secondary operational key-value caches, recreating the data synchronization and drift issues the architecture was designed to replace.

proposals.name: Synthetic Content Saturation Degenerating Organic Search Signal Capture
proposals.definition: Organic search visibility measurement and intent discovery have decoupled from buyer demand due to search engines surfacing AI-generated overviews and conversational answers.
proposals.why_unsolved: Search engines obscure referral click-stream and prompt-level impression data, making attribution of conversational zero-click brand appearances impossible to measure deterministically.
proposals.evidence: SEO and content marketing teams report dramatic drops in organic referral tracking while direct navigational searches and brand-query lift run disconnected from traditional SERP rankings.

proposals.name: Consent Drift Across Decentralized First-Party Data Ecosystems
proposals.definition: Customer privacy choices made across multiple touchpoints become out of sync across streaming, edge caches, third-party SaaS tools, and downstream clean rooms in real time.
proposals.why_unsolved: Consent management platforms operate via asynchronous API syncs rather than unified event-driven transactional semantics, resulting in propagated latency where revoked consent is violated during the propagation window.
proposals.evidence: Regulatory enforcement actions around delayed opt-out enforcement continue to rise despite full adoption of tier-one consent management tooling.
